title: Chapter 4 Quiz 8
description: Grouping values of different types under one name.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **record**?
options: A group of cells of one type
A table of rows and columns
A set of records on a disk drive
A group of fields of mixed types
questions.explanation: A record groups related fields, for example a student's name, age and average. Watch out: a group of cells of one type is an array.

questions.question: How is a record different from an array?
options: A record is read by an index number
A record can hold only strings
A record's fields can differ in type
A record is always larger than an array
questions.explanation: Array: same type, access by index. Record: possible different types, access by field name.

questions.question: How do we access the field Name of the record variable Student?
questions.explanation: Fields are reached with the dot operator. Watch out: square brackets are for array indexes.

questions.question: Complete the declaration of a record type.
questions.code:
TYPE STUDENTS = {{1}}
    Name: string
    TD, TP: Real
{{2}} RECORD

questions.question: Elements that make up a record are called {{1}}.
questions.explanation: The elements of a record are its fields.

questions.question: Why use a record for a student (name, first name, two grades) rather than four separate arrays?
options: Four arrays are not allowed in a program
One structure keeps a student's data together
Records are always faster than arrays
Arrays cannot store strings at all
questions.explanation: With several arrays, the data of one entity is scattered. Watch out: arrays can store strings, and four arrays are allowed, but they are awkward.

questions.question: Which of these can be fields of a record?
questions.explanation: Fields can be of any data type.

questions.question: Which declares an array of 4 students of record type Student?
questions.explanation: The array's element type is the record type.

questions.question: Match each structure to its main feature.
right: Different types, accessed by field name
Data kept on disk after the program ends
questions.explanation: The three kinds of structure in this chapter.

questions.question: This should read the name and the age of a student. One line has an error.
questions.code:
TYPE STUDENT = RECORD
    Name: string
    Age: integer
END RECORD
Declare Student As STUDENT
Read(Student.Name)
Read(Student[Age])
questions.explanation: A field is reached with the dot: Student.Age. Watch out: Student[Age] is the syntax of an array index.

questions.question: A class has 20 students, and each record has 4 fields. How many values are stored in total?
questions.explanation: 20 records × 4 fields = 80. Watch out: the values are multiplied, not added (24).
